name: Autoimmune Hepatitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Simplified International Autoimmune Hepatitis Group (IAIHG) Criteria 2008

criteria.description: ANA or SMA >= 1:40 (1 point), >= 1:80 or anti-LKM1 >= 1:40 (2 points)
Elevated IgG above upper limit of normal (1 point), >= 1.1x ULN (2 points)
Liver histology compatible with AIH: interface hepatitis (1 point), typical of AIH (2 points)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Score >= 6 (probable AIH) or >= 7 (definite AIH) on simplified criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Type 1 AIH: ANA and/or SMA positive; most common form. Type 2 AIH: anti-LKM1 and/or anti-LC1 positive; more common in children. Anti-SLA/LP is the most specific antibody for AIH.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Interface hepatitis on liver biopsy with plasma cell infiltration
pathognomonic.notes: Histologic hallmark; plasma cell-rich infiltrate at the portal-parenchymal interface

rare.notes: More common in Type 2 AIH and children

rare.symptomName: Overlap syndrome features (PBC or PSC overlap)

laboratory: Elevated ALT and AST (often markedly elevated; hepatocellular pattern)
Negative viral hepatitis serologies (HAV, HBV, HCV, HEV)
imaging: Liver ultrasound: hepatomegaly, heterogeneous parenchyma, signs of portal hypertension
Transient elastography (FibroScan): elevated liver stiffness indicating fibrosis
genetic: HLA-DR4 (DRB1*0401) - later onset, more treatment responsive
other: Liver biopsy: interface hepatitis, plasma cell-rich portal infiltrate, hepatocyte rosetting, emperipolesis
Liver biopsy: fibrosis staging (Metavir or Ishak scoring)

distinguishingFeatures: Beading of bile ducts on MRCP

redFlags: Acute liver failure with encephalopathy and coagulopathy
INR >1.5 with bilirubin elevation suggesting severe disease
Signs of portal hypertension at presentation (varices, ascites)
Failure to respond to corticosteroid therapy (consider overlap or alternative diagnosis)
Development of hepatocellular carcinoma in cirrhotic patients
references: Hennes EM, et al. Simplified criteria for the diagnosis of autoimmune hepatitis. Hepatology. 2008;48(1):169-176.
Mack CL, et al. Diagnosis and Management of Autoimmune Hepatitis in Adults and Children: 2019 Practice Guidance and Guidelines from AASLD. Hepatology. 2020;72(2):671-722.
European Association for the Study of the Liver. EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines: Autoimmune hepatitis. J Hepatol. 2015;63(4):971-1004.
